one_liner: Senior TSA headquarters media relations and strategic communications advisor who writes public-facing materials, handles reporters, and counsels leadership on sensitive, high-visibility issues.
fit_summary: This is a GS-14-equivalent role that requires one full year of GS-13-level experience leading media and stakeholder communications, drafting press releases and talking points, and advising senior leadership on strategic communications. Daniel's policy knowledge, people skills, and emergency-management consulting background at IEM are relevant, but nothing on file shows a senior communications or public affairs role. Daniel qualifies only if the IEM work truly involved leading communications at that level.
eligibility: Open to the public; U.S. citizenship or national status is required.

You need 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to GS-13, and it must cover all three areas: leading external outreach and advising on messaging; drafting and coordinating press releases, statements, talking points, and speeches; and developing strategic communications plans while advising senior leadership.
You must obtain and maintain a Secret clearance and complete a favorable background investigation; Selective Service registration is required if applicable.
Travel is listed inconsistently: the requirements say at least 50%, but the summary field says 5. Confirm with HR before applying.
You must pass the USA Hire competency assessments at or above the cut score to be considered.
strategy: Before applying, honestly list what you did at IEM. Only claim the GS-14 level if you can point to a full year of work that hits all three specialized-experience elements; otherwise target GS-11/12 public affairs postings (01035) at TSA, FEMA, or DHS.

If the IEM work included communications, frame it as communications in emergency management: preparedness messaging, recovery outreach to government clients and communities, and briefing materials for agency leadership.

Write a two-page USAJOBS resume. For each job, include dates, hours per week, and title, then add one short paragraph mapping directly to each of the three specialized-experience elements, using the posting's exact words.
Preview the questionnaire at the link in the posting. Answer 'expert' only where your resume shows proof, because overstating can remove you from consideration.
Prepare for the USA Hire assessment, which covers interpersonal skills, influencing/negotiating, reasoning, and stress tolerance. Set aside uninterrupted time to complete it.
The posting opens October 16 and closes October 30, 2026. Submit several days early and attach transcripts only if you use education toward qualifying.
resume_bullets: Drafted and coordinated [number] [press releases/talking points/briefing materials] on [disaster recovery/preparedness topic] for [client agency] leadership, ensuring accuracy and consistency across [channels].
Led outreach to [types of stakeholders, e.g., local officials, community organizations, industry partners] for [program], advising [client leadership role] on messaging for [high-visibility issue].
Developed a [timeframe] communications plan for [program], tracking [metrics] and reporting results to [audience].
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you advised senior leaders on how the media or public would react to a controversial policy.
How would you build relationships with national reporters covering TSA screening issues?
Walk us through how you would develop and measure a national communications campaign.
Describe handling a high-pressure, fast-moving communications situation, such as a disaster or crisis.
watch_outs: The GS-13-equivalent specialized experience bar is high, and Daniel's communications seniority is unverified.
The 50% travel requirement conflicts with the posting's travel field of 5; clarify with HR.
The Secret clearance and background investigation add time before you could start.
The application window is only two weeks.
